Title (original English): Hydrologic and hydraulic analyses of selected streams in Richland County, Ohio
TRL assessment unit: Richland County HEC-RAS flood-analysis model
TRL rationale: The Clear Fork Mohican River model was calibrated to 16 flood events and used to produce water levels and inundation boundaries for selected flood frequencies.

Title (original English): Hydrologic and hydraulic analyses of selected streams in Stark County, Ohio
TRL assessment unit: Hydrologic and hydraulic models for 14 streams in Stark County
TRL rationale: Streamgage records, regional regression equations, and surveyed cross sections were combined over approximately 50 miles to calculate flood levels and regulatory floodways.

Title (original English): Hydrologic and hydraulic analyses of selected streams near the city of Rittman in Wayne and Medina Counties, Ohio
TRL assessment unit: HEC-RAS application for four streams near Rittman
TRL rationale: Observed flows and survey data were combined over 36.2 miles to produce inundation boundaries, and the supporting data were released.

Title (original English): Monitoring fine-sediment volume in the Colorado River ecosystem, Arizona: construction and analysis of digital elevation models
TRL assessment unit: Colorado River repeat-survey and sediment-volume DEM workflow
TRL rationale: Six field campaigns in 2000–2004 produced DEMs for 11 reaches, with vertical uncertainty quantified by data type.

Title (original English): Channel mapping of the Colorado River from Glen Canyon Dam to Lees Ferry in Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Arizona
TRL assessment unit: Colorado River integrated bathymetric/topographic surveying and DEM production workflow
TRL rationale: Multiple sensor datasets collected along an actual 15.84-mile river reach in 2013–2016 were integrated to produce a DEM, substrate maps, and uncertainty estimates.

Title (original English): Water-quality variability and constituent transport and processes in streams of Johnson County, Kansas, using continuous monitoring and regression models, 2003-11
TRL assessment unit: Johnson County continuous water-quality monitoring and regression-estimation system
TRL rationale: Continuous observations and sample-based regression were used to estimate water quality and loads in five major watersheds during 2003–2011.

Title (original English): Estimation, distribution, and development of a surrogate model for Escherichia coli in the New River, New River Gorge National Park and Preserve, West Virginia, 2021–23
TRL assessment unit: New River turbidity-based E. coli surrogate model
TRL rationale: A regression model was developed from field samples and continuous measurements collected in 2021–2023, with an adjusted coefficient of determination of 0.556.

Title (original English): Development of a regionally consistent geospatial dataset of agricultural lands in the Upper Colorado River Basin, 2007-10
TRL assessment unit: Upper Colorado agricultural-land and irrigation-status mapping workflow
TRL rationale: State agricultural-land datasets and 1-meter aerial imagery were combined to classify approximately 1.76 million acres. Irrigation-method classifications were compared with an independent assessment.

Title (original English): Simulation of daily streamflow for nine river basins in eastern Iowa using the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System
TRL assessment unit: PRMS models for nine eastern Iowa river basins
TRL rationale: Satisfactory daily-flow performance was reported at 57 of 79 calibration sites and 13 of 14 separate validation sites.

Title (original English): Simulation of daily streamflow for 12 river basins in western Iowa using the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System
TRL assessment unit: PRMS models for 12 western Iowa river basins
TRL rationale: Models were calibrated at 42 streamgages, with satisfactory daily-flow performance reported at 36 sites.

Title (original English): Estimating flow-duration statistics and low-flow frequencies for selected streams and the implementation of a StreamStats web-based tool in Puerto Rico
TRL assessment unit: Implementation of Puerto Rico low-flow regression equations in StreamStats
TRL rationale: Regression equations were developed from 28 streamgages and incorporated into the StreamStats web application.

Title (original English): P2S—Coupled simulation with the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System (PRMS) and the Stream Temperature Network (SNTemp) Models
TRL assessment unit: P2S software coupling PRMS and SNTemp
TRL rationale: A coupled program, installation package, source code, and example datasets establish that functional integration has been implemented.

Title (original English): seawaveQ—An R package providing a model and utilities for analyzing trends in chemical concentrations in streams with a seasonal wave (seawave) and adjustment for streamflow (Q) and other ancillary variables, version 2.0.0 (appendix 1: package vignette)
TRL assessment unit: Regression-analysis workflow in the supplied 2020 seawaveQ vignette
TRL rationale: Executable examples, model outputs using actual stream data, and previous applications support a reusable R analysis workflow.

Title (original English): Sediment monitoring and streamflow modeling before and after a stream restoration in Rice Creek, Minnesota, 2010–2019
TRL assessment unit: Rice Creek sediment monitoring and two-dimensional flow analysis for restoration assessment
TRL rationale: Ten years of field monitoring were combined with simulations before and after restoration. Parameters were tested against water-level errors.

Title (original English): Application of the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System (PRMS) to simulate the streamflows and water balance of the Red River Basin, 1980–2016
TRL assessment unit: Red River PRMS water-budget model
TRL rationale: A basin model was implemented for 1980–2016, but acceptable accuracy was achieved at only 36% and 26% of evaluation streamgages for monthly and daily flows, respectively. This supports limited validation with field data.

Title (original English): Simulation of future streamflow and irrigation demand based on climate and urban growth projections in the Cape Fear and Pee Dee River Basins, North Carolina and South Carolina, 2055–65
TRL assessment unit: Cape Fear and Pee Dee SWAT future-streamflow and irrigation-demand models
TRL rationale: Two minimally calibrated historical basin models achieved median monthly NSE values of 0.53 and 0.61 and were used for future scenarios.

Title (original English): Monitoring and simulation of hydrology, suspended sediment, and nutrients in selected tributary watersheds of Lake Erie, New York
TRL assessment unit: Lake Erie tributary SWAT water-quality and load models
TRL rationale: Samples from 19 sites and rloadest estimates supported nine watershed models. Management scenarios were applied to seven calibrated models.

Title (original English): Development of a two-dimensional hydraulic model for the Kalamazoo River between the Trowbridge and Allegan City Dams, Michigan
TRL assessment unit: Kalamazoo River two-dimensional hydraulic model
TRL rationale: The 9.2-mile model was calibrated against measured water levels and velocities. Reported water-level RMSE values of 0.20 and 0.32 ft demonstrate performance at the actual reach scale.

Title (original English): Parameter estimation at the conterminous United States scale and streamflow routing enhancements for the National Hydrologic Model infrastructure application of the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System (NHM-PRMS)
TRL assessment unit: NHM continental-scale calibration and Muskingum routing enhancement
TRL rationale: Multistage calibration was applied to 109,951 HRUs and 1,417 streamgages, and two routing algorithms were tested.

Title (original English): Remediation scenarios for attenuating peak flows and reducing sediment transport in Fountain Creek, Colorado, 2013
TRL assessment unit: Fountain Creek flood and sediment-transport scenario models
TRL rationale: Rainfall-runoff, hydraulic, and sediment models were calibrated with field observations and evaluated using separate streamgages and flood events.

Title (original English): Water quality in the Anacostia River, Maryland and Rock Creek, Washington, D.C.: Continuous and discrete monitoring with simulations to estimate concentrations and yields of nutrients, suspended sediment, and bacteria
TRL assessment unit: Anacostia and Rock Creek continuous-monitoring water-quality and load models
TRL rationale: Regression equations and LOADEST were applied to field samples and continuous measurements, with constituent-specific coefficients of determination reported.

Title (original English): Simulation of natural flows in major river basins in Alabama (appendix 1 only)
TRL assessment unit: Simulated-versus-observed flow comparisons in the supplied Alabama natural-flow appendix
TRL rationale: Station-specific monthly/daily flow comparisons and scatterplots establish limited model evaluation against actual observations.

Title (original English): A precipitation-runoff model for simulating natural streamflow conditions in the Smith River watershed, Montana, water years 1996-2008
TRL assessment unit: Smith River PRMS natural-streamflow model
TRL rationale: The model was calibrated for 2002–2007 and evaluated separately for 1996–2001, demonstrating its ability to reproduce conditions at the scale of an actual watershed.

Title (original English): Simulation of streamflow and the effects of brush management on water yields in the Double Mountain Fork Brazos River watershed, western Texas 1994–2013
TRL assessment unit: Double Mountain Fork SWAT streamflow and brush-management model
TRL rationale: Calibration for 1994–2008 was separated from validation for 2009–2013. An NSE of 0.71 was reported for the study period.

Title (original English): Preliminary synthesis and assessment of environmental flows in the middle Verde River watershed, Arizona
TRL assessment unit: Verde River environmental-flow assessment tool combination
TRL rationale: A three-year study and a five-site field pilot evaluated model suitability, but monthly streamflow estimates were inadequate for determining environmental flows.

Title (original English): Flood hydrology and dam-breach hydraulic analyses of five reservoirs in Colorado
TRL assessment unit: Colorado five-reservoir dam-breach risk simulation
TRL rationale: Existing data and regression-based design floods were used to configure HEC-HMS and HEC-RAS and evaluate scenarios for five dams.

Title (original English): Network global navigation satellite system survey to harmonize water-surface elevation data for the Rainy River Basin
TRL assessment unit: Rainy River GNSS water-level datum harmonization survey
TRL rationale: Three field crews collected simultaneous reference-mark observations, independently processed by U.S. and Canadian agencies to harmonize operational water-level data.

Title (original English): Method for estimating potential wetland extent by utilizing streamflow statistics and flood-inundation mapping techniques: Pilot study for land along the Wabash River near Terre Haute, Indiana
TRL assessment unit: Wabash River potential-wetland mapping pilot
TRL rationale: A 14-mile pilot combined seven-day flow statistics, an inundation surface, and a DEM to demonstrate potential-wetland mapping.

Title (original English): Processing of next generation weather radar-multisensor precipitation estimates and quantitative precipitation forecast data for the DuPage County streamflow simulation system
TRL assessment unit: DuPage County radar and rainfall-forecast processing pipeline
TRL rationale: An hourly observation database and NWS forecasts were integrated into a near-real-time streamflow system being tested in an actual watershed operating environment.

Title (original English): A stormwater management model for the West Branch Brandywine Creek, Chester County, Pennsylvania
TRL assessment unit: West Branch Brandywine rainfall-runoff model
TRL rationale: Only Modena was both calibrated and verified. Coatesville was calibrated but not verified, and Honeybrook could not be calibrated.

Title (original English): Historical floods and geomorphic change in the lower Little Colorado River during the late 19th to early 21st centuries
TRL assessment unit: Hydraulic reconstruction of historical Little Colorado River floods
TRL rationale: High-water marks and long-term records were integrated, and the hydraulic model was calibrated by comparing water levels at three peak flows.

Title (original English): Floodwater drainage assessment of Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, 2020–22
TRL assessment unit: Hydrologic and hydraulic diagnosis of drainage problems at Offutt Air Force Base
TRL rationale: Field observations from 2020–2022 were combined with HEC-RAS and flow-duration analysis to investigate backwater-related drainage problems.

Title (original English): Development of a flood-warning system and flood-inundation mapping in Licking County, Ohio
TRL assessment unit: Licking County streamgage and inundation-map flood-warning system
TRL rationale: Streamgages were installed or reinstalled, and calibrated inundation maps were supplied to the NWS to connect the warning system to an operational environment.

Title (original English): Development of flood-inundation maps for the Mississippi River in Saint Paul, Minnesota
TRL assessment unit: Saint Paul Mississippi River inundation-map service
TRL rationale: Twenty-five mapped stages were provided through USGS and NWS services after rating-curve calibration and verification against 2011 flood high-water marks.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for the Hoosic River, North Adams and Williamstown, Massachusetts, from the confluence with the North Branch Hoosic River to the Vermont State line
TRL assessment unit: Hoosic River inundation-map and forecast application
TRL rationale: Eight maps were produced following calibration to streamgage relations and Irene high-water marks and were published on the USGS website.

Title (original English): Flood Map for the Winooski River in Waterbury, Vermont, 2014
TRL assessment unit: Winooski River flood-map and streamgage application
TRL rationale: Hydraulic analysis incorporating the Irene flood produced two types of maps made available through the USGS inundation-mapping service.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for the Green River in Colrain, Leyden, and Greenfield, Massachusetts, from U.S. Geological Survey streamgage 01170100 Green River near Colrain to the confluence with the Deerfield River
TRL assessment unit: Green River flood-frequency and inundation-map model
TRL rationale: Seven mapped stages were produced after calibration to Irene high-water marks and streamgage relations.

Title (original English): Development of a hydraulic model and flood-inundation maps for the Wabash River near the Interstate 64 Bridge near Grayville, Illinois
TRL assessment unit: Wabash River two-dimensional inundation-map and streamgage service
TRL rationale: Twenty-seven mapped stages, calibrated with two streamgages and GPS water levels, are available on the USGS website for use with real-time and forecast stages.

Title (original English): Hydraulic modeling and flood-inundation mapping for the Huron River and Ore Lake Tributary, Livingston County, Michigan
TRL assessment unit: Huron River and Ore Lake inundation-map application
TRL rationale: Calibration to a streamgage and temporary water-level sensors yielded an RMSE of 0.68 ft, and maps were provided through FIM.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps of the Meramec River from Eureka to Arnold, Missouri, 2018
TRL assessment unit: Meramec River inundation maps linked to observations and forecasts
TRL rationale: Map libraries for different Mississippi River levels were produced after calibration to 2015–2016 high-water marks and streamgage relations.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for a 23-mile reach of the Medina River at Bandera, Texas, 2018
TRL assessment unit: Medina River inundation-map service
TRL rationale: Twenty-nine mapped stages were delivered through FIM following calibration to the 2018 rating curve and independent validation with four flood events.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for Nimishillen Creek near North Industry, Ohio, 2019
TRL assessment unit: Nimishillen Creek inundation-map application
TRL rationale: Calibration to a rating curve and 2017 high-water marks yielded an RMSE of 0.31 ft. Maps were provided through FIM.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for the North Platte River at Scottsbluff and Gering, Nebraska, 2018
TRL assessment unit: North Platte River inundation-map application
TRL rationale: Ten mapped stages calibrated to the 2018 stage-discharge relation are available through USGS FIM.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for Dardenne Creek in St. Charles County, Missouri, 2019
TRL assessment unit: Dardenne Creek inundation mapping with backwater effects
TRL rationale: Models were calibrated to streamgage rating curves and 2015 high-water marks, and maps for Mississippi River backwater conditions were provided online.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for the Little Calumet River from Lansing to South Holland, Illinois, 2020
TRL assessment unit: Little Calumet River unsteady-flow inundation-map application
TRL rationale: Historical flow and rating-curve data from three streamgages were evaluated to produce 24 mapped stages available online.

Title (original English): Precipitation-driven flood-inundation mapping of the Little Blue River at Grandview, Missouri
TRL assessment unit: Little Blue River coupled rainfall-runoff and inundation model
TRL rationale: HEC-HMS and HEC-RAS were calibrated to the May 2020 flood to produce maps for land-cover and moisture scenarios.

Title (original English): Precipitation-driven flood-inundation mapping of Muddy Creek at Harrisonville, Missouri
TRL assessment unit: Muddy Creek precipitation-driven inundation model
TRL rationale: Multiple 2019 and 2021 events were used for calibration, with a separate 2021 event used for validation before evaluating rainfall and channel-condition scenarios.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps created using a synthetic rating curve for a 10-mile reach of the Sabinal River and a 7-mile reach of the West Sabinal River near Utopia, Texas, 2021
TRL assessment unit: Sabinal and West Sabinal synthetic-rating-curve inundation model
TRL rationale: A synthetic curve constrained by the 2002 peak stage supported 35 mapped stages, with comparisons meeting the stated tier B error criterion.

Title (original English): Flood-inundation maps for 14.8 miles of Little and Big Papillion Creeks in Omaha, Nebraska, 2023
TRL assessment unit: Papillion Creeks inundation-map and streamgage application
TRL rationale: Map libraries calibrated to 2022 stage-discharge relations are provided through USGS FIM for use with real-time observations.

Title (original English): Flood-Inundation Maps of the Current and Jacks Fork Rivers including the Ozark National Scenic Riverways, Southeast Missouri, 2023
TRL assessment unit: Current and Jacks Fork Rivers multi-reach inundation-map system
TRL rationale: One- and two-dimensional models calibrated with eight reference streamgages and high-water loggers produced maps available online.

Title (original English): Areas contributing recharge to production wells and effects of climate change on the groundwater system in the Chipuxet River and Chickasheen Brook Basins, Rhode Island
TRL assessment unit: Chipuxet and Chickasheen groundwater recharge-area model
TRL rationale: Calibrated groundwater and water-budget models used parameter covariance and Monte Carlo analysis to assess uncertainty in well-contributing areas.

Title (original English): Simulating hydrologic response to climate change scenarios in four selected watersheds of New Hampshire
TRL assessment unit: Climate-response models for four New Hampshire watersheds
TRL rationale: Four actual-watershed test cases were evaluated using flow statistics, NSE, and NRMSE over a 31-year calibration period.

Title (original English): Simulated hydrologic response to climate change during the 21st century in New Hampshire
TRL assessment unit: Statewide New Hampshire PRMS climate-response model
TRL rationale: A statewide hydrologic model and climate scenarios were developed, with present/future results evaluated using calibration statistics.

Title (original English): Assessment of Columbia and Willamette River flood stage on the Columbia Corridor Levee System at Portland, Oregon, in a future climate
TRL assessment unit: Columbia and Willamette future-flood hydraulic models
TRL rationale: Two two-dimensional models reproduced the 1996 and 1997 floods, reporting RMSE values of 0.085–0.32 m and NS values above 0.96.

Title (original English): Estimated groundwater recharge from a water-budget model incorporating selected climate projections, Island of Maui, Hawai‘i
TRL assessment unit: Maui climate-scenario water-budget model
TRL rationale: Daily simulations used 2017 land cover and present/future climate inputs to estimate recharge for the island's 25 aquifer systems.

Title (original English): Streamflow response to potential changes in climate in the Upper Rio Grande Basin
TRL assessment unit: Upper Rio Grande PRMS climate-response model
TRL rationale: An actual-basin naturalized-flow model was developed and calibrated, showed improved performance over the initial NHM, and was applied to future conditions.

Title (original English): Estimated groundwater recharge for mid-century and end-of-century climate projections, Kaua‘i, O‘ahu, Moloka‘i, Lāna‘i, Maui, and the Island of Hawai‘i
TRL assessment unit: Six-island Hawaii future-groundwater-recharge water-budget model
TRL rationale: Daily water budgets and detailed climate scenarios were applied to six islands and 110 aquifer systems, using runoff relations based on regional observations.

Title (original English): Simulating present and future groundwater/surface-water interactions and stream temperatures in Beaver Creek, Kenai Peninsula, Alaska
TRL assessment unit: Beaver Creek coupled SWB–MODFLOW 6–SNTEMP model
TRL rationale: A physically based coupled model using groundwater levels, flows, and temperatures from 2019–2023 reported a mean stream-temperature error of 0.15°C.

Title (original English): Simulation of daily streamflows at gaged and ungaged locations within the Cedar River Basin, Iowa, using a Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System model
TRL assessment unit: Cedar River PRMS daily-flow model
TRL rationale: Calibration and validation periods and uncalibrated sites were distinguished. Adequate simulation was reported at four of six uncalibrated sites.

Title (original English): Hydrologic model of the Modesto Region, California, 1960-2004
TRL assessment unit: Modesto MODFLOW-OWHM integrated hydrologic model
TRL rationale: The model was calibrated to 4,061 groundwater levels and 2,739 monthly flows, with reproduction of 1960–2004 trends evaluated.

Title (original English): Calibration of Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System (PRMS) to simulate prefire and postfire hydrologic response in the upper Rio Hondo Basin, New Mexico
TRL assessment unit: Rio Hondo PRMS prefire/postfire hydrologic model
TRL rationale: Models were separately calibrated against observations before the fire in 2007–2012 and after it in 2014–2015, with statistically satisfactory performance reported.

Title (original English): Evaluation of hydrologic simulation models for fields with subsurface drainage to mitigated wetlands in Barnes, Dickey, and Sargent Counties, North Dakota
TRL assessment unit: North Dakota SPAW–DRAINMOD wetland model combination
TRL rationale: Models were applied at three field sites and evaluated against water-depth errors, but calibration centered on 2018 and performance in wetter or drier years could not be evaluated.

Title (original English): Development of an integrated hydrologic flow model of the Rio San Jose Basin and surrounding areas, New Mexico
TRL assessment unit: Rio San Jose integrated hydrologic model
TRL rationale: The integrated model was calibrated against 12 observation groups. Streamflow observations from 1983 and 2018 were withheld for verification.

Title (original English): Simulation of climate-change effects on streamflow, lake water budgets, and stream temperature using GSFLOW and SNTEMP, Trout Lake Watershed, Wisconsin
TRL assessment unit: Trout Lake coupled GSFLOW–SNTEMP model
TRL rationale: The coupled model was calibrated with 1998–2007 levels, flows, evapotranspiration, and snowpack, plus high-resolution stream temperatures from 2002.

Title (original English): Application of the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System (PRMS) in the Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint River Basin in the southeastern United States
TRL assessment unit: ACF Basin PRMS hydrologic model
TRL rationale: Calibration/evaluation with 35 streamgages produced daily-flow NS values above 0.6 at 31 sites, demonstrating basin-scale simulation.

Title (original English): Application of the Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System (PRMS) to simulate near-native streamflow in the Upper Rio Grande Basin
TRL assessment unit: Upper Rio Grande PRMS natural-streamflow model in the actual PDF
TRL rationale: A parameter-transfer method was implemented for 1,021 HRUs and validated in three of nine near-native subbasins.

Title (original English): A model for evaluating stream temperature response to climate change in Wisconsin
TRL assessment unit: Wisconsin SWB–ANN stream-temperature model
TRL rationale: Validation at 67 independent sites explained 76% of daily mean stream-temperature variation, and the model was applied to the statewide stream network.

Title (original English): Methods for estimating selected low-flow frequency and mean annual flow statistics at gaged and ungaged locations on streams in Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina
TRL assessment unit: Southeastern U.S. low-flow regressions and StreamStats linkage
TRL rationale: Regional regressions and errors based on observed flows are documented, but the report contains both completed and planned wording for StreamStats integration.

Title (original English): The effects of Missouri River mainstem reservoir system operations on 2011 flooding using a Precipitation-Runoff Modeling System model
TRL assessment unit: Missouri River PRMS model removing reservoir-regulation effects
TRL rationale: Regulated and unregulated flows for the 2011 flood were compared, with statistical support for monthly and annual high-flow estimates.

Title (original English): Monitoring recharge in areas of seasonally frozen ground in the Columbia Plateau and Snake River Plain, Idaho, Oregon, and Washington
TRL assessment unit: Seasonally frozen-ground remote sensing and PRMS recharge simulation
TRL rationale: Satellite and field observations were combined, and runoff, frozen-ground conditions, and future recharge responses were evaluated in two PRMS watersheds.

Title (original English): User guide to Exploration and Graphics for RivEr Trends (EGRET) and dataRetrieval: R packages for hydrologic data
TRL assessment unit: EGRET and dataRetrieval hydrologic-analysis software
TRL rationale: Integrated data retrieval, WRTDS analysis, and graphics are supported by detailed installation/use guidance and cross-validation procedures.

Title (original English): Spatially distributed groundwater recharge for 2010 land cover estimated using a water-budget model for the Island of O‘ahu, Hawai‘i
TRL assessment unit: O‘ahu spatial recharge model in the actual PDF
TRL rationale: An island-scale daily water budget used observed runoff relations from 17 basins to evaluate average and drought conditions.

Title (original English): Simulation of potential groundwater recharge for the glacial aquifer system east of the Rocky Mountains, 1980–2011, using the Soil-Water-Balance Model
TRL assessment unit: Glacial aquifer SWB recharge model
TRL rationale: Calibration to base flow in 39 watersheds achieved an NSE of 0.94 and RMSE of 1.28 in/yr for mean annual targets.

Title (original English): Potential groundwater recharge rates for two subsurface-drained agricultural fields, southeastern Minnesota, 2016–18
TRL assessment unit: Comparison of agricultural-field recharge methods for Minnesota in the actual PDF
TRL rationale: WTF, DRAINMOD, and SWB methods were applied to two years of observations from two agricultural fields, with water-level performance compared.

Title (original English): Estimating spatially and temporally varying recharge and runoff from precipitation and urban irrigation in the Los Angeles Basin, California
TRL assessment unit: Los Angeles watershed recharge/runoff model including urban irrigation
TRL rationale: The model was calibrated to six streamgages and used to calculate actual-scale watershed water budgets for 1915–2014.

Title (original English): Analysis for agreement of the Northern Gulf of Mexico topobathymetric digital elevation model with 3-Dimensional Elevation Program 1/3 arc-second digital elevation models
TRL assessment unit: Northern Gulf TBDEM–3DEP agreement-assessment workflow
TRL rationale: Elevation differences and seams in regional DEMs were compared, reporting 95–100% agreement for 85% of the TBDEM elevation data.

Title (original English): One-meter topobathymetric digital elevation model for Majuro Atoll, Republic of the Marshall Islands, 1944 to 2016
TRL assessment unit: Majuro integrated 1-meter topobathymetric DEM workflow
TRL rationale: A multisensor DEM was validated using more than 70,000 GNSS points and lidar bathymetry, with land RMSE of 0.197 m reported.

Title (original English): Development of a numerical model to simulate groundwater flow in the shallow aquifer system of Assateague Island, Maryland and Virginia
TRL assessment unit: Assateague three-dimensional groundwater and salinity model
TRL rationale: A model using actual-island geological and spatial data was calibrated through inverse parameter estimation.

Title (original English): Nutrient budgets, marsh inundation under sea-level rise scenarios, and sediment chronologies for the Bass Harbor Marsh estuary at Acadia National Park
TRL assessment unit: Bass Harbor nutrient-budget and marsh-change analysis
TRL rationale: LOADEST and terrain analysis were applied to 2011–2012 field water-quality/hydrologic observations, with sensor calibration and verification.

Title (original English): Numerical modeling of the effects of Hurricane Sandy and potential future hurricanes on spatial patterns of salt marsh morphology in Jamaica Bay, New York City
TRL assessment unit: Jamaica Bay Delft3D coupled storm, vegetation, and sediment model
TRL rationale: Sandy field observations of water levels, waves, and marsh deposition supported calibration and validation before future hurricane simulations.

Title (original English): A one-dimensional diffusion analogy model for estimation of tide heights in selected tidal marshes in Connecticut
TRL assessment unit: Connecticut tidal-marsh one-dimensional diffusion-analogy model
TRL rationale: Field-data calibration and a GIS application are documented, with limited validation showing a maximum error of 0.3 ft.

Title (original English): The hydrologic system of the south Florida peninsula—Development and application of the Biscayne and Southern Everglades Coastal Transport (BISECT) model
TRL assessment unit: South Florida BISECT coupled surface-water, groundwater, and salinity model
TRL rationale: TIME and Biscayne models were integrated and refined. Levels, flows, salinity, and water temperature were compared with field data before management-scenario simulations.

Title (original English): Simulated effects of sea-level rise on the shallow, fresh groundwater system of Assateague Island, Maryland and Virginia
TRL assessment unit: Assateague sea-level-rise groundwater scenario model
TRL rationale: A three-dimensional model of the actual island and observations from 32 wells were used to assess freshwater responses to sea-level rise.

Title (original English): Simulation of water-table and freshwater/saltwater interface response to climate-change-driven sea-level rise and changes in recharge at Fire Island National Seashore, New York
TRL assessment unit: Fire Island MODFLOW-NWT–SWI2 groundwater model
TRL rationale: An existing SEAWAT model was converted to SWI2, automatically recalibrated, and applied to sea-level and recharge changes under actual-island conditions.

Title (original English): Development of a process-based littoral sediment transport model for Dauphin Island, Alabama
TRL assessment unit: Dauphin Island Delft3D littoral sediment model
TRL rationale: Waves, water levels, velocities, flows, and shoreline positions were evaluated through hindcasts and observations.

Title (original English): Forecasting storm-induced coastal flooding for 21st century sea-level rise scenarios in the Hawaiian, Mariana, and American Samoan Islands
TRL assessment unit: Pacific island coastal-inundation downscaling model
TRL rationale: Storm and sea-level scenarios were calculated at full scale along 1,870 km of coast, with an adopted numerical flooding error of ±0.5 m.

Title (original English): Moderate flood level scenarios—Synthetic storm-driven flood-inundation maps for coastal communities in 10 New Jersey counties
TRL assessment unit: New Jersey synthetic-storm inundation maps in FDST
TRL rationale: Map libraries associated with 25 real-time tide gages were provided through FDST, integrating them into a decision-support tool.

Title (original English): Database and time series of nearshore waves along the Alaskan coast from the United States-Canada border to the Bering Sea
TRL assessment unit: Alaska coastal SWAN downscaled wave database
TRL rationale: Time series for 1979–2019 were reconstructed from nine domains and 2,500 sea states and validated against observed waves.

Title (original English): Monitoring storm tide and flooding from Hurricane Sandy along the Atlantic coast of the United States, October 2012
TRL assessment unit: Sandy storm-tide field monitoring and data-delivery system
TRL rationale: Actual Sandy response included deployment at 224 locations and continuous recording of storm tide, documenting mission execution.

Title (original English): Monitoring storm tide and flooding from Hurricane Irma along the U.S. Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, and the Southeastern United States, September 2017
TRL assessment unit: Irma storm-tide sensor deployment, retrieval, verification, and publication system
TRL rationale: Sensors were deployed at 249 locations during an actual hurricane. Retrieved data were published and checked against high-water marks.

Title (original English): Beach morphology monitoring in the Elwha River Littoral Cell, 2004-2009
TRL assessment unit: Elwha repeat coastal topographic/bathymetric monitoring
TRL rationale: RTK-DGPS surveys and data processing were operated on the actual coast repeatedly during 2004–2009.

Title (original English): National assessment of nor’easter-induced coastal erosion hazards: mid- and northeast Atlantic coast
TRL assessment unit: Nor’easter probabilistic coastal-erosion assessment model
TRL rationale: An existing storm-impact approach was extended to nor’easters and evaluated at actual scale through a 2015 storm hindcast.

Title (original English): National assessment of shoreline change: historical shoreline change along the Pacific Northwest coast
TRL assessment unit: Pacific Northwest national shoreline-change workflow
TRL rationale: DSAS 4.2 and lidar were applied at 50-meter transect spacing to calculate regional change rates with datum-bias and uncertainty treatment.

Title (original English): Using a Bayesian Network to predict shore-line change vulnerability to sea-level rise for the coasts of the United States
TRL assessment unit: U.S. coastal Bayesian Network erosion-probability model
TRL rationale: Hindcast performance was compared with observed shoreline changes, but exact most-likely-outcome success rates varied markedly by region, from 34% to 98%.

Title (original English): National assessment of shoreline change: historical change along the north coast of Alaska, U.S.-Canadian border to Icy Cape
TRL assessment unit: Alaska national shoreline-change calculation workflow
TRL rationale: Historical shorelines were compared through a national assessment workflow to estimate rates and uncertainty at 26,567 transects.

Title (original English): Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) version 5.1 user guide
TRL assessment unit: DSAS v5.1 core shoreline-change rate calculations
TRL rationale: The released version underwent compatibility testing with ArcGIS 10.4–10.7 and has detailed installation, editing, and calculation guidance.

Title (original English): Monitoring of wave, current, and sediment dynamics along the Chincoteague living shoreline, Virginia
TRL assessment unit: Little Toms Cove oyster-castle field structures
TRL rationale: Installed structures were monitored for two winter months in 2019 to measure wave, circulation, and sediment responses.

Title (original English): The Surge, Wave, and Tide Hydrodynamics (SWaTH) network of the U.S. Geological Survey—Past and future implementation of storm-response monitoring, data collection, and data delivery
TRL assessment unit: Expanded SWaTH monitoring and data-delivery system
TRL rationale: More than 900 sites were surveyed/prepared, combining permanent monitoring, temporary sensors, and the STN data system.

Title (original English): Modeling of depth to base of Last Glacial Maximum and seafloor sediment thickness for the California State Waters Map Series, eastern Santa Barbara Channel, California
TRL assessment unit: Santa Barbara seafloor-sediment GIS interpolation workflow
TRL rationale: Actual survey lines and geological structure were used to estimate sediment thickness and volume, with seafloor-depth differences evaluated.

Title (original English): Oregon OCS seafloor mapping: Selected lease blocks relevant to renewable energy
TRL assessment unit: Oregon OCS seafloor survey and habitat-mapping workflow
TRL rationale: Multibeam and video surveys at an actual offshore candidate site were integrated with existing data, and video was used to validate sonar interpretations.
